title: 2025年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

P2 The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music.

P3 A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

P4 Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

P5 Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

questions.q: What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world?
options: They still make their presence felt.
They have given way to electronic music.
They will not fade away from the public eye.
They are no longer relevant to teenagers' lives.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world? 用 think of 直接问作者看法，对象又是全文核心话题，是典型的整体态度题。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author think of …，think of sth = 对某事物的看法；in today's world 是时间地点状语，限定评价的时间范围。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world? A) They still make their presence felt. B) They have given way to electronic music. C) They will not fade away from the public eye. D) They are no longer relevant to teenagers' lives.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 both opera and classical music are now still quite alive ↔They still make their presence felt 四个选项里只有 They still make their presence felt 与预判「仍有存在感」的肯定立场 吻合，其余三项要么表否定立场、要么改换主语。 B) 与原文相反 P1 只列举 pop music, jazz, and electronic music 作为崛起的对手，没说古典乐和歌 剧已 give way to（让位给）电子乐。 C) 无中生有 原文 started to fade away from the public eye 是已发生的事实，选项 They will not fade away from the public eye 把它改成对将来的否定预言，是无中生有的预言。 D) 以偏概全 you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon 只是承认青少年不常听，但作者用 Granted（诚然）让步后立刻 but 反转，重点 不在青少年身上。 关于当前制作的大部分流行音乐,我们了解到什么? A) 许多古典音乐爱好者可能难以欣赏它。 B) 它可以被视为古典音乐精致化的一个标志。 C) 它比古典音乐更微妙地迎合社会的音乐品味。 D) 它包含与某些古典音乐杰作相似的元素。

questions.q: What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced?
options: It can be difficult for many classical music fans to appreciate.
It can be seen as an indicator of refinement on classical music.
It caters to society's taste in music in a more subtle way than classical music.
It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced? 是对某具体 对象的客观信息提问，不带 infer/imply，按细节题处理。

【拆句】much of the popular music currently produced 是名词短语：much of 限定范围（大部 分），currently produced 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 popular music = 当下被制作 出来的流行音乐。后置分词定语是四级长难句高频结构，识别它能避免把 produced 误读成 谓语。

【定位】The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. 古典乐在当今社会重要性的最显著标志是：当下被制作出来的大部分流行乐使用了与古典乐 一些最佳作品相似的节拍、和声与旋律。 52. What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced? A) It can be difficult for many classical music fans to appreciate. B) It can be seen as an indicator of refinement on classical music. C) It caters to society's taste in music in a more subtle way than classical music. D) It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说的是「不学乐理的人难以察觉这一现象」，没说流行乐让古典乐迷难以欣赏。 B) 过度推断 原文只说流行乐「使用相似要素」，并未称其是古典乐的 refinement（精炼/提升）。 C) 张冠李戴 原文是「交响乐对社会音乐品味的影响是 subtle 的」，主语是交响乐的影响、不是流 行乐。 D) ✓ 正确 uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works ↔It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music 选项 D 把 similar 与 some of classical music's best works 都原样保留，仅把并列名 词上位为 elements，是定位句的标准同义替换。 作者为什么提到摇滚歌剧的发明? A) 为了说明如何用音乐讲述故事。 B) 为了给出歌剧最简单的定义。 C) 为了展示歌剧和古典音乐的相关性。 D) 为了证明在歌剧中使用管弦乐队的必要性。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera?
options: To illustrate how to tell a story using music.
To present the simplest definition of opera.
To show the relevance of opera and classical music.
To justify the necessity of using orchestras in opera.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera? 直接问举例的目 的，是例证目的题的最典型句式。

【拆句】题干主干 Why does the author mention X？X = the invention of the rock opera，of 短语作 the invention 的后置定语。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. 歌剧与古典乐仍具相关性的一个更佳例证，可以从摇滚歌剧的发明中看出。 53. Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera? A) To illustrate how to tell a story using music. B) To present the simplest definition of opera. C) To show the relevance of opera and classical music. D) To justify the necessity of using orchestras in opera.

【选项】A) 答非所问 Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form 只是为了 说明摇滚歌剧的合理性而插入的歌剧定义，不是举摇滚歌剧的目的。 B) 以偏概全 段中确实给了歌剧的最简定义，但那是为论证服务的工具，不是举摇滚歌剧的目的。 C) ✓ 正确 A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera ↔To show the relevance of opera and classical music 原文已把例子的服务对象 the relevance of opera and classical music 写在前置位置， 选项 C 用不定式 to show 把这个目的复述出来，是逐字命中。 D) 过度推断 原文只说 sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself ——是 sometimes（有时），不是 necessity（必要性）。 为什么古典音乐作品仍被用作现代电影的背景音乐? A) 电影制作人可选择的音乐类型很少。 B) 它们被认为是最具表现力的音乐类型。 C) 它们受到世界各地电影爱好者的好评。 D) 它们对于电影成为世界最受欢迎作品至关重要。

questions.q: Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies?
options: There are few types of music for movie producers to choose from.
They are considered to be the most expressive type of music.
They are well received by movie fans from all over the world.
They are essential for movies to become the world's greatest hits.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies? 是对一个具体事实问原因，答案在原文有直接对应，按细节题处理。

【拆句】题干主干 Why are classical music pieces still used as background music ...？被动语态 are used，still 表「仍然」，in modern movies 是地点状语。识别 are used 是被动而非 主动是关键，能避免把题理解成「古典乐使用了什么」。

【定位】Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. 古典乐迷也会告诉你，没有多少类型的音乐比它更具表现力。所以，古典乐至今仍被用作现 代电影的背景音乐就一点也不意外了。 54. Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies? A) There are few types of music for movie producers to choose from. B) They are considered to be the most expressive type of music. C) They are well received by movie fans from all over the world. D) They are essential for movies to become the world's greatest hits.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文从未说「电影制作方可选的音乐类型很少」，only 谈古典乐自身的表现力强。 B) ✓ 正确 there are few types of music that are more expressive ↔ They are considered to be the most expressive type of music 题干问 why，定位句的 So 前那句被替换为最高级表达，正好回答原因；这是唯一与原 因句对应的选项。 C) 因果颠倒 原文 These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans 是讲电影 配乐的结果——观众接受——并未说这是它被选作配乐的原因。 D) 张冠李戴 Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas 谈的是摇滚歌剧 的成就，与电影配乐被使用的原因无关。 关于我们的现代音乐,我们了解到什么? A) 如果没有古典音乐和歌剧作为基础,它不可能产生。 B) 它在对当今社会的影响方面无法超越古典音乐和歌剧。 C) 它在音乐爱好者中不会像古典音乐和歌剧那样受欢迎。 D) 在未来几个世纪里,它在重要性上可能无法与古典音乐和歌剧匹敌。

questions.q: What do we learn about our modern music?
options: It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation.
It cannot outcompete classical music and opera in its impact on our current society.
It will not enjoy as much popularity as classical music and opera among music fans.
It might not be able to rival classical music and opera in importance for centuries to come.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about our modern music? 是对 modern music 的客观信息提问，按 细节题处理；但因对象是全文性概念，定位句多落在尾段总结。

【拆句】题干主干 What do we learn about our modern music？our modern music 是介词宾 语，about 引出谈论对象。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. 古典乐与歌剧正是我们现代音乐所赖以建立的根基。 55. What do we learn about our modern music? A) It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation. B) It cannot outcompete classical music and opera in its impact on our current society. C) It will not enjoy as much popularity as classical music and opera among music fans. D) It might not be able to rival classical music and opera in importance for centuries to come.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon ↔ It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation 选项 A 用「否定 + without」的常见同义改写技法，把肯定陈述变成必要条件，逻辑完 全等价，是定位句标准的同义替换。 B) 无中生有 原文从未拿现代音乐和古典乐/歌剧比对社会影响力的高下，仅强调古典乐和歌剧仍 重要。 C) 偷换概念 原文谈的是「根基」与「重要性」，不是受欢迎程度（popularity）的比较。 D) 过度推断 原文 we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come 只是肯定古典乐和歌剧的持久重要，没有否定现代音乐重要性。
